atoms.text: Ancient Greece was the first advanced civilisation in Europe, but it was never one big country. This was mainly because of how many mountains and islands there were.
The mountains made Greek cities isolated and difficult to reach as there were no developed roads at the time.
This resulted in the founding of many smaller city-states.

atoms.a: Why was ancient Greece not one big country?
Why were other cities difficult to reach?

atoms.b: Even though some city-((++states stats)) had large differences, most had a couple of things in common.
To honour their gods, city-states built ((++temples swimming_pools)) and held many festivals. These cultural rituals were very important to the ancient Greeks.
